in_arabic.name: ماشر
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من مَعْشَرٍ، جماعة من الناس يجتمعون في مكان
in_arabic.long_meaning: ماشر هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، مشتق من مَعْشَرٍ الذي يعني جماعة من الناس يجتمعون في مكان واحد. يدل على الاجتماع والتواصل بين الناس، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سياق الحديث عن الاجتماعات والجماعات. يستخدم هذا الاسم في الثقافة الإسلامية للإشارة إلى الشخص الذي يهتم بالتواصل الاجتماعي والتعايش مع الآخرين.

in_urdu.name: ماشر
in_urdu.meaning: اشتقاقی نام، معاشرتی گروہ، لوگوں کا اجتماع
in_urdu.long_meaning: ماشر ایک مذکر نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے معاشرتی گروہ یا لوگوں کا اجتماع۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیاء میں مسلمانوں کے बीच استعمال ہوتا ہے، خاص طور پر پاکستان اور بھارت میں۔ اس کا عربی جڑوں سے تعلق ہے اور اسلامی ثقافت میں اس کا استعمال لوگوں کے درمیان رابطے اور سماجی تعلقات کی اہمیت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: माशर
in_hindi.meaning: समाजिक समूह, लोगों का जमावड़ा, माशर नाम का अर्थ
in_hindi.long_meaning: माशर एक पुरुष नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है। इसका अर्थ है सामाजिक समूह या लोगों का जमावड़ा। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में उपयोग किया जाता है और यह नाम लोगों के बीच सामाजिक संबंधों और एकत्रीकरण की महत्ता को दर्शाता है। यह नाम अरबी मूल से है और इसका उपयोग इस्लामी परंपरा में किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: ماشر
in_pashto.meaning: د خلکو اجتماع، د معاشرې ډله، ماشر نوم معنی
in_pashto.long_meaning: ماشر د نارینه وو نوم دی چې د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی. د دې نوم مطلب د خلکو اجتماع یا د معاشرې ډله ده. دا نوم د افغانستان او پاکستان په پښتون ټولنو کې کارول کیږي. دا نوم د عربي ریشه لرونکی دی او په اسلامي کلتور کې د خلکو تر منځ د اړیکو او اجتماعي همغږۍ د ارزښت ښودنه کوي.

in_english.name: Maashar

in_english.long_meaning: Maashar is a masculine given name of Arabic origin, derived from the root 'm-ʿ-sh-r' which signifies a group of people gathering or assembling. This name holds significance in Islamic tradition, emphasizing the importance of social gatherings, community bonding, and collective identity. It reflects the value of unity and shared experiences within Muslim cultures.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Maashar" has historical and cultural significance in Islamic tradition as a term used to refer to a pilgrim or traveler, particularly those who embark on the annual Hajj journey to Mecca. The Arabic word "Maashar" signifies movement and travel, emphasizing the idea of a spiritual journey towards personal growth and enlightenment. It is a reminder of the Islamic value placed on travel and exploration, as well as the importance of making the journey to the holy city of Mecca at least once in a lifetime for those who are able.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Maashar" holds deep spiritual significance in the Islamic tradition, representing the journey of the soul towards a closer relationship with God. The Arabic word "Maashar" can be translated as "station," reflecting the idea that the spiritual journey is not a constant motion but a series of stops and moments of reflection, meditation, and connection with the divine. This name serves as a reminder of the importance of the present moment, encouraging individuals to focus on their current actions and intentions rather than their past or future. Ultimately, the name "Maashar" encapsulates the essence of the Islamic pilgrimage, symbolizing a transformative, personal, and spiritual journey towards a deeper connection with God and a more profound understanding of one's place in the universe.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hakam, The History of the Conquests of Spain, 950-961 AD The name Maashar carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Maashar ibn Dhi Yazan, the last ruler of the independent Berber kingdom of Ronda, resisted the advancing Muslim forces led by Almanzor until his capital was taken in 950 AD. Almanzor then pressed on towards the Balearic Islands, where Maashar had sought refuge, but was repulsed by the local inhabitants. In 961 AD, Maashar was finally defeated and killed.

historical_references.context: Maashar al-Bhajri was a prominent scholar and jurist from Baalbek, Lebanon, during the Ayyubid and Rashidun periods. He was a student of Ibn Rushd and a teacher of Ibn Taymiyyah. Maashar is known for his works on Islamic jurisprudence and theology, and his influence can be seen in the writings of later scholars such as Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyah and Ibn Hajar al-Haytami.
